headline: Broad-based growth lifts profit and full-year guidance
summary_short: TransDigm's quarter ended June 27, 2026 saw net sales rise 22.5% y/y to $2,741M (13% organic), GAAP EPS of $9.39 (+10.9% y/y), and net income of $539M, as the company raised full-year 2026 guidance for sales, EBITDA As Defined, and EPS.
summary_long: Net sales grew 22.5% y/y (13% organic) to $2,741M, with commercial aftermarket, commercial OEM, and defense all posting double-digit growth. EBITDA As Defined margin was 52.8% (vs 54.4% a year ago) on acquisition dilution, though management says base-business margins still expanded. GAAP net income rose 9.6% y/y to $539M ($9.39/share); adjusted EPS was $10.87 (+13% y/y). TransDigm repurchased $1.0B of stock this quarter ($1.8B YTD) and raised $1.5B of incremental debt in April. Cash fell to $2,773M q/q on buybacks and debt-funded M&A (Jet Parts Engineering/Victor Sierra, ~$2.2B). TransDigm raised FY2026 guidance for net sales, net income, EBITDA As Defined, and both GAAP and adjusted EPS, excluding the pending Prince & Izant acquisition.

drivers.explanation: All three market channels grew double-digit y/y (commercial aftermarket +17%); organic sales growth of 13% came from volume and price, not acquisitions.
Scaled with the 22.5% y/y revenue increase; gross margin was roughly flat (59.4% vs 59.5% a year ago per our own revenue/gross-profit data), so cost growth tracked sales growth.
Tracks the sales increase at a roughly stable gross margin; the release gives no additional gross-margin-specific narrative beyond the channel growth already cited for revenue.
Sales growth flowed through; the release's net-income narrative cites higher selling and administrative expense as a partial offset (interest expense, also cited, sits below the operating line).
Tracks operating income; not itemized as a separate line by the company, so the move mirrors the same sales-growth and SG&A drivers.
Company reports EBITDA of $1,345M for the quarter, up 20% y/y, consistent with the sales and margin drivers cited above; not further decomposed in the release.
Tracks operating income growth; the release notes higher interest expense (on the incremental April debt raise) as a partial offset below the operating line.
Company attributes the rise primarily to higher net sales and its value-driven operating strategy, partially offset by higher SG&A and interest expense.
Follows net income growth on a lower diluted share count (57.4M vs 58.1M a year ago, -1.2%) from buybacks, amplifying per-share growth above the net-income growth rate.
Reported as identical to basic EPS ($9.39) in the release; same drivers as EPS above — net income growth plus a reduced share count from buybacks.
Cash fell q/q as $1.0B of quarterly buybacks and continued M&A funding (Jet Parts Engineering/Victor Sierra, ~$2.2B) outpaced operating cash generation and the $1.5B April debt raise.
TransDigm completed a $1.5B incremental debt offering in April 2026 ($0.5B senior subordinated notes, $1.0B term loans), explaining the q/q and y/y increase.
not explained in the release beyond the same April $1.5B debt offering; the company does not break out which portion of new debt became current.

TransDigm's equity is structurally negative from its debt-funded special-dividend and buyback history; the wider deficit q/q and y/y tracks the incremental debt raise and $1.8B YTD buybacks, not a profitability change.
Reflects $1.0B of share repurchases this quarter (809,101 shares at an average $1,208), bringing YTD buybacks to $1.8B, per the release's share-repurchase disclosure.

CEO Mike Lisman frames the quarter as broad-based double-digit growth across aftermarket, OEM, and defense, with base-business margin expansion outside acquisition dilution; the company raised FY2026 guidance for sales, net income, EBITDA As Defined, and EPS, excluding the pending Prince & Izant deal.
